caption:
February 2006. A liquor store owner starts filming wine reviews in the back of the shop.

No audience. No budget. A cheap camera.

He kept going until 2011. One thousand episodes.

Over that stretch the family business went from $3M a year to $60M a year. Then he sold out of wine entirely and built an ad agency on what he'd learned.

Here's the part worth sitting with: for most of those five years, this did not look like a strategy. It looked like a guy talking about wine on the internet.

The compounding is invisible while it's happening. That's exactly why most people quit at month four — they're measuring week by week, and week by week it looks like nothing.

Content isn't a campaign you run. It's an asset that either compounds or doesn't exist.

The question isn't whether you can post for a month. It's whether you can still be posting when it finally starts working.

📌 Send this to someone who stopped posting in week six because "it wasn't doing anything."
